verses.greek: Οὕτως ἡμᾶς λογιζέσθω ἄνθρωπος ὡς ὑπηρέτας Χριστοῦ καὶ οἰκονόμους μυστηρίων θεοῦ.
verses.literal: So us should regard a man as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.
verses.dgt: Let a person regard us in this way: as servants of Christ and stewards of God’s mysteries.

verses.greek: ὧδε λοιπὸν ζητεῖται ἐν τοῖς οἰκονόμοις ἵνα πιστός τις εὑρεθῇ.
verses.literal: In this case moreover it is required in the stewards that faithful one may be found.
verses.dgt: Moreover, in this case it is required of stewards that one be found faithful.

verses.greek: ἐμοὶ δὲ εἰς ἐλάχιστόν ἐστιν, ἵνα ὑφʼ ὑμῶν ἀνακριθῶ ἢ ὑπὸ ἀνθρωπίνης ἡμέρας· ἀλλʼ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἀνακρίνω·
verses.literal: Me myself however to the smallest matter it is that by you I may be examined or by a human court In fact neither myself do I examine.
verses.dgt: But to me it is a very small thing that I should be examined by you or by a human court; indeed, I do not even examine myself.

verses.greek: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐμαυτῷ σύνοιδα, ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐν τούτῳ δεδικαίωμαι, ὁ δὲ ἀνακρίνων με κύριός ἐστιν.
verses.literal: No thing for against myself I have been conscious of yet not by this have I been justified the One however judging me the Lord is.
verses.dgt: For I am conscious of nothing against myself, but I am not justified by this; the one who examines me is the Lord.

verses.greek: ὥστε μὴ πρὸ καιροῦ τι κρίνετε, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ὁ κύριος, ὃς καὶ φωτίσει τὰ κρυπτὰ τοῦ σκότους καὶ φανερώσει τὰς βουλὰς τῶν καρδιῶν, καὶ τότε ὁ ἔπαινος γενήσεται ἑκάστῳ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.literal: So then not before the time anything do judge until when may have come the Lord who both will bring to light the hidden things the of darkness and will make manifest the motives of the hearts and then the praise will come to each from the God.
verses.dgt: So then do not judge anything before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and reveal the intentions of hearts; and then praise will come to each from God.

verses.greek: Ταῦτα δέ, ἀδελφοί, μετεσχημάτισα εἰς ἐμαυτὸν καὶ Ἀπολλῶν διʼ ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἐν ἡμῖν μάθητε τό· Μὴ ὑπὲρ ἃ γέγραπται, ἵνα μὴ εἷς ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἑνὸς φυσιοῦσθε κατὰ τοῦ ἑτέρου.
verses.literal: These things now brothers I have applied to myself and Apollos on account of you so that in us you may learn the not beyond what things has been written that not one for the one you be puffed up over the other.
verses.dgt: Now these things, brothers and sisters, I applied to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that in us you may learn the saying, “not beyond what is written,” so that none of you may be puffed up for one against another.

verses.greek: τίς γάρ σε διακρίνει; τί δὲ ἔχεις ὃ οὐκ ἔλαβες; εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔλαβες, τί καυχᾶσαι ὡς μὴ λαβών;
verses.literal: Who for you makes different? What now have you which not you did receive? If now even you did receive it why boast you as not having received it?
verses.dgt: For who makes you different? And what do you have that you did not receive? But if you received it, why do you boast as though you did not receive it?

verses.greek: Ἤδη κεκορεσμένοι ἐστέ, ἤδη ἐπλουτήσατε, χωρὶς ἡμῶν ἐβασιλεύσατε· καὶ ὄφελόν γε ἐβασιλεύσατε, ἵνα καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμῖν συμβασιλεύσωμεν.
verses.literal: Already satiated you are already you have been enriched apart from us you reigned and I wish that really you did reign so that also we ourselves you may reign with.
verses.dgt: Already you are filled! Already you became rich! Without us you began to reign! And I wish indeed that you had begun to reign, so that we also might reign with you.

verses.greek: δοκῶ γάρ, ὁ θεὸς ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ἐσχάτους ἀπέδειξεν ὡς ἐπιθανατίους, ὅτι θέατρον ἐγενήθημεν τῷ κόσμῳ καὶ ἀγγέλοις καὶ ἀνθρώποις.
verses.literal: I think for the God us the apostles last has exhibited as appointed to death because a spectacle we have become to the world both to angels and to men.
verses.dgt: For I think God displayed us, the apostles, last of all, as people sentenced to death, because we became a spectacle to the world, both to angels and to people.

verses.greek: ἡμεῖς μωροὶ διὰ Χριστόν, ὑμεῖς δὲ φρόνιμοι ἐν Χριστῷ· ἡμεῖς ἀσθενεῖς, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἰσχυροί· ὑμεῖς ἔνδοξοι, ἡμεῖς δὲ ἄτιμοι.
verses.literal: We ourselves are fools on account of Christ you yourselves however wise in Christ we ourselves weak you yourselves however strong You yourselves honored we ourselves however without honor.
verses.dgt: We are fools because of Christ, but you are wise in Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are honored, but we are dishonored.

verses.greek: ἄχρι τῆς ἄρτι ὥρας καὶ πεινῶμεν καὶ διψῶμεν καὶ γυμνιτεύομεν καὶ κολαφιζόμεθα καὶ ἀστατοῦμεν
verses.literal: As far as the present hour both we hunger and thirst and are poorly clad and are buffeted and wander homeless
verses.dgt: To this present hour we both hunger and thirst, and we are poorly clothed and beaten and homeless,

verses.greek: καὶ κοπιῶμεν ἐργαζόμενοι ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσίν· λοιδορούμενοι εὐλογοῦμεν, διωκόμενοι ἀνεχόμεθα,
verses.literal: and we toil working the with our own hands Being reviled we bless being persecuted we endure
verses.dgt: and we labor, working with our own hands. When insulted, we bless; when persecuted, we endure;

verses.greek: δυσφημούμενοι παρακαλοῦμεν· ὡς περικαθάρματα τοῦ κόσμου ἐγενήθημεν, πάντων περίψημα ἕως ἄρτι.
verses.literal: being defamed we entreat As the scum of the earth we have become of all the refuse until now.
verses.dgt: when slandered, we appeal gently. We have become like the refuse of the world, the scum of all things, until now.

verses.greek: Οὐκ ἐντρέπων ὑμᾶς γράφω ταῦτα, ἀλλʼ ὡς τέκνα μου ἀγαπητὰ νουθετῶν·
verses.literal: Not shaming you do I write these things but as children of mine beloved admonishing you.
verses.dgt: I do not write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.

verses.greek: ἐὰν γὰρ μυρίους παιδαγωγοὺς ἔχητε ἐν Χριστῷ, ἀλλʼ οὐ πολλοὺς πατέρας, ἐν γὰρ Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ διὰ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἐγὼ ὑμᾶς ἐγέννησα.
verses.literal: If for ten thousand guardians you shall have in Christ yet not many fathers in for Christ Jesus through the gospel I myself you begot.
verses.dgt: For even if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the good news.

verses.greek: παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς, μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε.
verses.literal: I exhort therefore you imitators of mine do become.
verses.dgt: Therefore I urge you: become imitators of me.

verses.greek: διὰ τοῦτο ἔπεμψα ὑμῖν Τιμόθεον, ὅς ἐστίν μου τέκνον ἀγαπητὸν καὶ πιστὸν ἐν κυρίῳ, ὃς ὑμᾶς ἀναμνήσει τὰς ὁδούς μου τὰς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, καθὼς πανταχοῦ ἐν πάσῃ ἐκκλησίᾳ διδάσκω.
verses.literal: On account of this I sent to you Timothy who is my child beloved and faithful in the Lord who you will remind of the ways of mine that are in Christ Jesus even as everywhere in every church I teach.
verses.dgt: For this reason I sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways in Christ Jesus, just as I teach everywhere in every assembly.

verses.greek: ὡς μὴ ἐρχομένου δέ μου πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐφυσιώθησάν τινες·
verses.literal: As to not coming now of me to you were puffed up some
verses.dgt: Now some became puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.

verses.greek: ἐλεύσομαι δὲ ταχέως πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐὰν ὁ κύριος θελήσῃ, καὶ γνώσομαι οὐ τὸν λόγον τῶν πεφυσιωμένων ἀλλὰ τὴν δύναμιν,
verses.literal: I will come however soon to you if the Lord wishes and I will find out not the talk of those puffed up but the power.
verses.dgt: But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will know not the speech of those who are puffed up, but their power.

verses.greek: οὐ γὰρ ἐν λόγῳ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλʼ ἐν δυνάμει.
verses.literal: Not for in word the kingdom the of God is but in power.
verses.dgt: For the kingdom of God is not in speech but in power.

verses.greek: τί θέλετε; ἐν ῥάβδῳ ἔλθω πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἢ ἐν ἀγάπῃ πνεύματί τε πραΰτητος;
verses.literal: What desire you? With a rod I may come to you or in love a spirit then of gentleness?
verses.dgt: What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?
